newsitem.title: FRANCE: Six bombs kill 18 in Algeria - papers.
newsitem.headline: Six bombs kill 18 in Algeria - papers.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas in Algeria ended a lull with six bombings that Algerian newspapers on Tuesday said killed at least 18 people and wounded scores.

A leading newspaper predicted more violence because of government attacks on guerrillas ahead of parliamentary elections that militant Islamists are barred from contesting. A wave of bombings and massacres around Algiers that ended in early February killed more than 300 people.
La Tribune newspaper reported three separate bombings on Monday in neighbourhoods in Algiers' southern Kouba district, a Moslem guerrilla stronghold.

A car bomb in Anasser neighbourhood killed four and wounding eight on Monday afternoon, it said. Another booby-trapped car exploded 45 minutes later on a highway by a van carrying army medical personnel near Jolie Vue area, killing four people, it said.
The third bomb exploded one and half hours later in a small bus in Ben Omar neighbourhood, killing three people and wounding eight, La Tribune added.

Another bomb exploded on Monday near a police station in the centre of the western town of Saida, killing seven people, El Watan newspaper said on Tuesday. Two bombs hit Sidi-Bel-Abbes, in western Algeria, causing serious damage but no casualties, said the newspaper Liberte.
El Watan, the best-informed newspaper on security matters, warned of more violence.
"The obsessive fear is settling again and we expect worse in the next days since the security forces have dealt serious blows to the armed groups, particulary in the capital," said El Watan.
More than 50 Moslem guerrillas were killed by security forces in Algiers and the western province of Relizane on Saturday, according to newspaper reports.
About 60,000 people had died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.

Algiers experienced its most deadly suicide attack in January 1995 when a rebel slammed an explosives-laden car into the gate of the main police station, killing more than 40 people and wounding about 300.
The North African country, without an elected parliament for five years, is to hold June 5 legislative elections that exclude Islamist parties.
